provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: B2b family batch, rfq archetype. Shops serve both industry and homeowners, so the site carries two doors. Welding certifications stay as bracketed placeholders. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: On-site welding for trailers, loader buckets, gates and structural steel, what the welding rig carries, the travel radius and how call-out time is billed
pageStructurePlus.why: A broken trailer hitch or a cracked bucket can't come to the shop. Buyers with equipment down decide on whoever shows a mobile rig and a callback time.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Railings, stair stringers, gates, range hoods, fire pits and custom furniture frames, with how a homeowner or designer starts a job and the typical lead time
pageStructurePlus.why: Homeowners and designers search for custom metal work differently from plant buyers. A separate door keeps the industrial page clean and still catches them.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Mild steel, stainless and aluminum, and the finishes on offer: powder coat, galvanizing, paint, brushed or raw with clear coat, and which finishes go out to a partner
pageStructurePlus.why: Finish drives cost and lead time more than the welding does. Buyers who see finish options up front send a complete request.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How repeat brackets, frames and guards are reordered by part number, which jigs and fixtures the shop keeps on file, and batch sizes it takes
pageStructurePlus.why: Plant maintenance buyers come back for the same part. Showing a reorder path turns a one-off fabrication job into a standing account.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What can be welded back and what should be replaced: cracked frames, worn cutting edges, hardfacing, hitch and axle repair, with a photo intake for the break
pageStructurePlus.why: Repair buyers want a yes or no before they haul a machine in. A clear repair-versus-replace page saves both sides a trip.

designDirections.name: Shop Door
designDirections.bestFor: One- and two-welder shops doing repair, gates, trailers and walk-in jobs
designDirections.whyItFits: Brick and Linen's slab type reads like a stamped shop sign, which suits a small welding shop that sells on craft and a callback.

designDirections.name: Fab Spec
designDirections.bestFor: Fabrication shops quoting contractors, plants and equipment dealers
designDirections.headlineSample: Custom metal fabrication for {City} contractors and plants
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo. Gunmetal with an arc-orange accent and mono labels fits process lists, material thickness and lead times.

designDirections.name: Made in Steel
designDirections.bestFor: Architectural fabricators selling stairs, railings and feature metalwork to designers and builders
designDirections.whyItFits: Noir Editorial gives finished steel and real shop photos a dark gallery, which is how designers and architects judge custom fabrication.

openers.line: Your welding shop's Google listing has hours and a phone number but no website, so a plant buyer who needs a guard fabricated can't see what metal you work or how big a job you take.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What a fabrication buyer would find behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing links to Facebook, where the custom gates sit next to trailer repairs and shop dog posts. A contractor looking for a fabricator wants the processes and materials in one place.
openers.hook: Tap the Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note one industrial and one residential post.
openers.linkLine: Both sides of the welding shop, on one site: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing still runs on a free host with a contact form that doesn't send. A buyer with a drawing to quote gives a fab shop one try.
openers.hook: Open the site and test the form or look for a builder banner or an old year. Note what you find.
openers.linkLine: Same fab shop, with a form that delivers: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone your welding site's gallery loads sideways and the call button is off the screen. Mobile welding customers search from beside a broken trailer.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your welding site, working on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.angle: No way to send a drawing
openers.line: There's no way to send your shop a sketch or a DXF except texting your cell. A request page that takes the drawing, the metal and the quantity would bring in cleaner fabrication jobs.
openers.hook: Check any site and the listing for an upload or quote form. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A fabrication request that takes the drawing: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your stair stringers and powder-coated railings are better work than most fab shops post, and they scroll away on Instagram in a week.
openers.hook: Find one finished metal piece in their posts. Name it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your metalwork on a project page that stays put: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention welding a cracked frame the same day. A farm or contractor in a hurry would read that before calling anyone else, if it were on a site.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about speed or a specific repair. Quote it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your repair reviews next to the mobile welding page: {demo-link}

openers.line: When planting or harvest starts, equipment breaks and farmers search for a mobile welder that afternoon. The welding shops they find on their phones get the repairs.
openers.hook: Use this in rural or farm areas a few weeks before the local planting or harvest season. Name the season.
openers.linkLine: A mobile welding page ready for the busy season: {demo-link}

openers.line: A trailer hitch snaps on a Saturday and the owner searches for a welder who can come out. If your shop's line rings out after five, that job goes to the next rig.
openers.hook: Call their number after hours or on a weekend. Note whether it rings out or goes to voicemail.
openers.linkLine: A welding page that takes the breakdown call after hours: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw the post that your shop is hiring a welder. Good welders size up a fab shop online before they apply, and so do the contractors who send you work.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or a job listing. Note the date and whether it's still open.
openers.linkLine: A fabrication shop site with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your truck rig shows up at job sites across the county, but nothing says how far your mobile welding goes. A contractor two towns over has no idea you'd come.
openers.hook: Look for posts showing the rig at sites in other towns. Name the furthest one.

openers.line: Custom gates and railings take weeks and real steel, and homeowners ask about deposits and payment before they commit. A fab page that explains your deposit terms saves the awkward call.
openers.hook: Only if they do residential custom work. Check posts for gates, railings or furniture first.
openers.linkLine: Custom metal work with deposit terms explained: {demo-link}

openers.line: General contractors ask a welding sub for a certificate of insurance before they let a rig on site. A page that says you're insured for field welding gets you past that check faster.
openers.hook: Look for 'insured' on their listing or posts. Never claim coverage or certifications you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and field welding details on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: It sounds like your fabrication work comes from a few contractors and the farm down the road. When their buyer changes, the new one searches for a metal shop instead of asking around.
openers.hook: Look for reviews or posts that thank a repeat customer or a contractor. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a new buyer finds your fab shop: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is real fabrication. A piece like that belongs on a page a contractor can send to their client before they ask you for a price.
openers.hook: Pick their newest welding or fabrication post and name it: the piece, the metal and the finish.
openers.linkLine: That metal job on a project page: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is good fabrication.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found social pages, but nowhere a contractor could send a drawing or a homeowner could see your gates and railings. I put together a sample welding shop page with a drawing request and a mobile welding section, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it help if I sent it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my last message got lost in the shop. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a fabrication request that takes a drawing, a mobile welding page with your travel radius, and a separate door for custom residential metal work. If it's not useful, say so and I'll leave you alone.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for welding and fabrication shops here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"No surprise, you're under a hood all day. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with a drawing upload, a mobile welding page and a gallery for your custom metal work, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a shop your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, about what one set of custom railings brings in."
"Can I show you for ten minutes this week, at lunch or after you shut the shop?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: I've got more welding work than I can handle.
objections.handler: "Then the site picks which work you get. A drawing request with metal and quantity lets you turn down the small stuff and keep the fabrication jobs that pay."

objections.objection: My customers just text me pictures.
objections.handler: "Keep that. The request page gives them a place to send the picture plus the metal, size and deadline, so you aren't texting back five questions."

objections.objection: Contractors find me through other contractors.
objections.handler: "They still look you up before handing you a structural job. The site shows them your processes and insurance before they ask."

objections.objection: My nephew can make me a website.
objections.handler: "He probably can. What I add is the fab request that asks the right questions and a mobile welding page that ranks for breakdown searches. I can hand him the layout if you'd rather."

objections.objection: Half my work is homeowners, half is industrial. One site won't fit.
objections.handler: "That's why it has two doors: one for plants and contractors with drawings, one for gates and railings with a gallery. Same shop, two front counters."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's a drawing request, a mobile welding page and two galleries. That's about one custom gate."

email.subject: Fabrication request page for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for welding and fab shops in {City}, and I made a sample site for {Business Name} with a drawing upload. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} welding demo down on Friday to make room.

Want me to keep it up? One word either way is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — contractors around {City} are lining up fabrication subs for the spring build season. Thought of you.

The welding shop site is still here whenever you want it, and the price hasn't changed. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to one custom railing or gate job, not to a day of mobile repair.
The fabrication request with drawing upload is the core. Price the rest as additions to it.
Price the residential metalwork gallery by project count, not page count.
Charge for the mobile welding page and its coverage pages separately; they chase a different search than fabrication.
Keep the monthly add-ons below a few hours of shop rate so a slow month never makes them a question.
Quote the repeat parts library only when they already reorder the same part for a plant.

lineItems.description: Max with metal, thickness, quantity, finish, deadline and multi-file upload for drawings and site photos.
Max with a radius map, what the rig carries, call-out billing and a breakdown request that texts the owner.
Max when each project carries the metal, finish, dimensions and a short build note.
Max with powder coat colour cards, galvanizing and stainless notes and lead time effects per finish.
Max with a private part list per customer, reorder by part number and quantity breaks.
Max with machine type, break location, photo upload and a haul-in or come-out choice.

whatElseYouSell.name: Shop and rig photo day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One afternoon shooting the welding bays, the rig and finished steel gives the fab site real pictures instead of none."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on a day with finished pieces waiting for pickup.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for welding and fab
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each week a new repair or fabrication job goes on your Google profile, tagged mobile welding or custom metal, so both searches find you."

whatElseYouSell.name: Contractor and plant buyer outreach
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short monthly note to the maintenance managers and GCs near your shop, showing a recent fabrication job and the drawing request."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the request page has a few real jobs behind it.

whatElseYouSell.name: Rig and truck lettering artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Your welding rig parks at job sites all week. Lettering with the mobile welding number and the site address works every hour it's parked."

whatElseYouSell.name: Designer and architect lookbook
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short printed and PDF book of your railings, stairs and feature metal to leave with interior designers and builders."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once there are enough residential metal projects to fill it.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after repairs
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After every same-day welding repair, the customer gets a short review request while they're still relieved."

whatElseYouSell.name: Harvest and planting season campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Before planting starts, a campaign to farms near the shop: mobile welding, hardfacing and a number to save."
whatElseYouSell.when: A few weeks before the local planting or harvest season, in farm areas only.

withoutAI.whoPays: The coater, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Who powder coats your gates and railings? Coaters need a colour chart and a drop-off page as much as you needed a site."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Coaters depend on fab shops for work and listen when a regular customer recommends you.

withoutAI.route: The steel service center they buy from
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your steel supplier sells to every welding shop in the area with a stock list nobody can search. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Service centers have budgets, and their counter customers are your next prospect list.

withoutAI.whoPays: The installer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The fence company you build ornamental gates for needs a site that sells those gates. I'll build it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: They resell the shop's fabrication, so a better installer site means more metal orders.

withoutAI.route: Trailer dealers and farm equipment shops
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The trailer dealer who sends you hitch and frame repairs has an inventory page from years ago. You can get me in the door."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Dealers trust the welder who keeps their customers rolling, and they have inventory sites worth rebuilding.

withoutAI.route: General contractors who sub structural steel
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The GC who subs you the stair and lintel work has a projects page nobody updates. A welding sub's introduction gets me a meeting."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: GCs need project portfolios to win bids, and the fab shop sees their projects first-hand.

withoutAI.route: Interior designers who spec custom metal
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The designer who sent you that hood and railing has a portfolio stuck in a PDF. Introduce me and I'll put it online."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Designers who spec custom fabrication care about portfolio sites and trust the makers they use.

withAI.route: Colour and finish quote assistant for the coater
withAI.pitchLine: "Fab shops and homeowners upload part photos and sizes, and the coater gets a draft powder coat quote by surface area and colour."
withAI.whyItWorks: Coaters quote dozens of small parts a week. A draft quote saves them hours, and the welding client sends them traffic.

withAI.route: Stock and cut-list assistant for the steel supplier
withAI.pitchLine: "Fab shops paste in a cut list, and the assistant matches it to the supplier's stock lengths and drafts the order."
withAI.whyItWorks: It keeps shops ordering from one service center, which the center values more than a discount.

withAI.route: Gate and railing configurator for the fence installer
withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners describe the gate opening and style, and the fence installer gets a draft ornamental gate quote with the fab shop's pricing."
withAI.whyItWorks: It sells the welding client's metal through someone else's customers.

withAI.route: Repair triage assistant for the trailer dealer
withAI.pitchLine: "Dealer customers describe a cracked trailer frame or broken hitch, and the assistant sorts it into warranty, dealer repair or the welding shop."
withAI.whyItWorks: Dealers want fewer service calls, and the welding client is already where the hard repairs go.

withAI.route: Bid summary assistant for the general contractor
withAI.pitchLine: "The GC drops in plan sets and gets a summary of the miscellaneous metals scope to send to fab subs."
withAI.whyItWorks: GCs lose time pulling steel scopes from drawings, and the fab client proves the scope is right.

withAI.pitchLine: "The designer describes a custom metal piece, and the assistant drafts a spec sheet with metal, finish and dimensions for the fabricator."
withAI.whyItWorks: Designers send cleaner requests, and the welding client gets jobs that are easier to quote.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for breakdown repairs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Someone calls about a broken trailer while you're welding, gets a text asking where it is and what cracked, and you call back knowing whether to load the rig."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the shop number forwarded and wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Fabrication quote calculator by weight and hours
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the steel, the weld length and the finish, and it drafts the fabrication quote from your shop rate and material markup."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their shop rate, material markup, finish costs and a few past quotes to check against.

softwareAI.name: Drawing-to-cut-list helper
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload a customer's sketch or PDF drawing, and it drafts the steel cut list and weld notes for you to check before quoting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs a set of past drawings with the cut lists they produced. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job board for the shop floor
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every fabrication job on one screen: cut, weld, finish, out for coating, ready for pickup, so nobody asks the owner where a part is."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their job steps and a screen in the shop.

softwareAI.name: Pickup-ready texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a gate or bracket comes back from powder coat, the customer gets a text that it's ready, with shop hours."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, with the job board. Needs customer phone numbers on each job.

softwareAI.name: Quote writer from shop-floor voice notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Talk through the welding job at the bench, and a clean written quote with scope, metal and lead time is ready to send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs past quotes and their standard terms. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Repeat parts portal for plant customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Plant buyers log in, see the brackets and guards you've made them before, and reorder by part number without a drawing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, once a plant reorders the same part twice. Needs part drawings and prices for each repeat customer.

softwareAI.name: Repair photo triage
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers upload a photo of the cracked frame or bucket, and it sorts the welding repair into shop, mobile or replace for you to confirm."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the repair intake and a few hundred past repair photos with the owner's call. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Steel price update on open quotes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When your steel supplier's price changes, every open fabrication quote older than two weeks gets flagged for a recheck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the quote calculator and a price sheet from their supplier.

softwareAI.name: Material offcut inventory
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Log the plate, tube and angle offcuts in the rack, and the quote calculator checks them before you order new metal."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs a weekend to log the rack and a phone at the saw.

softwareAI.name: Mobile welding dispatch map
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Breakdown calls drop on a map with the rig's location, so the owner can stack nearby field welding jobs into one trip."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, once mobile work is a steady share. Needs the rig's phone and the job list.

softwareAI.name: Weld procedure and job notes search
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A welder asks how the shop handled that stainless rail last spring, and gets the owner's job notes and settings instead of guessing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs written job notes and procedures the owner approves. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing per fabrication order
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which fabrication jobs made money once steel, consumables, coating and welder hours are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs hours and material per job for a few months.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot for metal and finish questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'do you weld aluminum' and 'how long for a powder-coated railing' from your real shop answers, then takes the drawing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their service list, finishes and lead times. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Invoicing with deposit and balance reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Custom metal jobs get a deposit invoice at approval and a balance reminder the day the piece is ready."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their accounting system and deposit terms.

softwareAI.name: Residential project tracker for homeowners
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners waiting on a custom gate or railing see where it is: drawn, cut, welded, coated, install date."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, with the shop job board. Needs residential jobs flagged on the board.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for welding customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every review about a fab job or a roadside weld gets a reply drafted in your voice, ready to approve between jobs."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with the review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Bid notice watcher for miscellaneous metals
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It reads local bid boards and plan rooms each week and flags railings, stairs and miscellaneous steel packages your shop can quote."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the boards they use and the job sizes they want. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Bilingual helper and welder screening
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Welder and helper applicants answer the shop's questions on processes and positions in their language, and you only call the ones who fit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they're hiring. Needs must-haves, pay range and shift. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Shop safety and inspection log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Daily checks on the welding leads, gas cylinders, hoods and extinguishers logged on a phone, ready when a customer's safety team asks."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their current checklist and who signs it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the fab quote calculator for welding shops
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a fabrication quote calculator for one shop. Every small welding shop prices steel on a calculator and a guess."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first shop taught you the quoting math and paid for it. Every metro has dozens of shops with the same problem.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Shop finder licensed to a welding supply distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Put a find-a-welder map on your site for every fab shop that buys gas and wire from your branches."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Gas and wire distributors already spend on shop loyalty. Sending shops jobs keeps them buying.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member fab shop a drawing request page and a capability template as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewal reasons, and one deal reaches many welding shop owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each mobile welding territory needs a breakdown request that routes to the nearest rig. I build the template once."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract, many territories, one template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Vendor portal for a plant's maintenance department
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every outside fab shop and machine shop sends quotes and drawings into one portal tied to your work orders."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Plants juggle dozens of small metal vendors. The welding client's reorder workflow proves you understand it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label fab shop template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency lands welding clients and starts from a blank page. License my fabrication template with the drawing request built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell them the part you already perfected.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Same welding kit in the next county
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New fab shop clients in a new area
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one welding and fabrication shop per area. {City} is taken. The next county is open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the template, the pitch and the shop as proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your trailer owners need frame and hitch repair near home. A map of vetted welding shops cuts your warranty calls."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers want repairs handled close to the owner, and the welding client is the first vetted shop.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your members need mobile welding at harvest. A member services page with vetted repair shops keeps them in the co-op."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Co-ops sell member value, and rural welders are the service members miss most.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Railing and stair estimator sponsored by fab shops
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners estimate a metal railing or stair from length and style, and the sponsoring welding shop gets the request."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: It uses only the sponsor's own rates, so it never claims market data, and sends the sponsor ready buyers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Someone started your quoting or shop-floor tool and disappeared. I've already built that fabrication workflow."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded clients already decided to buy. They need someone who knows the shop workflow.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Trade school welding programme placement page
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your welding graduates need shops to hire them. A placement page listing local fab shops fills both sides."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Schools are measured on placements, and the welding client is a hiring shop with a story to tell.

upsellLadder.offer: Welding shop site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The welding site and the care plan go on one contract, so adding a new process or a new gallery is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review requests and Google profile upkeep
upsellLadder.trigger: A month live, and a same-day welding repair customer has left a thank-you.
upsellLadder.line: "That customer whose trailer you fixed on a Saturday is the review the next breakdown search needs."

upsellLadder.trigger: The gallery is still running on placeholders and a big fabrication job is about to ship.
upsellLadder.line: "That stair is leaving the shop next week. Let's shoot it, and the welding bays, before it goes."

upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of drawing requests show they're quoting the same kinds of brackets, gates and frames.
upsellLadder.line: "Half your requests are the same few metal jobs. A calculator drafts those quotes before you finish your coffee."

upsellLadder.offer: Job board for the shop floor
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a customer asking where their part is, or a job that sat at the coater.
upsellLadder.line: "Nobody should have to call you to find a part. The fab board shows every job's step."

upsellLadder.offer: Repeat parts portal for plant customers
upsellLadder.trigger: A plant reorders the same welded part for the second time.
upsellLadder.line: "That plant just reordered the same guard. Give them a portal and they'll never shop the part around."

upsellLadder.trigger: The residential metalwork gallery passes a dozen finished projects.
upsellLadder.line: "You've got enough railings and stairs for a book. Designers keep printed metalwork books on the desk."
